The app sends a POST request exactly to the address in the “Server address” field, including the path and parameters. The request body contains the whole backup file, without multipart or JSON wrapping. The content type is application/octet-stream, the length is known in advance and sent in the Content-Length header. Both http and https are supported, the app waits up to one minute for a response

X-Backup-Name: the file name for saving the backup, in the format remember-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM with the backup extension. The time is taken from the phone. Do not use the name as a path: the server should remove all characters except letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore.\n\nAuthorization: Bearer with the token is sent only if a token is set in the app. The server compares it with its own and responds with 401 without saving the backup if they do not match

Any 2xx code (200, 201, 204) means the backup is saved, and the app records the time in “Last backup on the server”. The response body is not read. Any other code or a lost connection is treated as an error: its text appears under the button, and a scheduled attempt is repeated later

This is the same file as in a manual export: the database, its key and photos, encrypted with the backup password. The server cannot and should not read it, only store it. The backup is restored with a regular import in the app using the same password. Each upload creates a new full file, the server removes old backups itself if needed

Manually, the backup is sent with “Send a backup now”. On schedule, it is sent once every specified number of days when the phone has a network connection. Android picks the exact time to save battery, so a backup may arrive a few hours later. If sending fails, the system retries later

The backup is always encrypted, so its contents are not accessible even over http. However, over http the token is sent in plain text, so use https for a server reachable from the internet. The backup password and token are stored on the phone in encrypted form, the key is kept in the phone’s secure chip
